Using approximately 3.0 inverse femtobarns of 8 TeV proton-proton collision data collected by the LHCb detector, the effective $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ lifetime ($\tau_{\text{eff}}$) has been measured. This value, determined to be 44.9 times 10 to the negative 15 seconds, is derived from the product of the true $B^0_s$ meson lifetime and its transverse momentum-averaged squared value. The result incorporates corrections for both finite track impact parameter resolution and physical decay, yielding a statistical precision of 1.3%.

This study examines the directionality of cosmic rays exceeding 4 EeV, utilizing a comprehensive dataset from the Pierre Auger Observatory that surpasses 1000 events and covers the celestial sphere up to 120 degrees from the galactic center. The analysis reveals a pronounced anisotropy in the energy spectrum exceeding 10 EeV, characterized by a dipole amplitude of 37% pointing toward (RA, Dec) = (201.78, 17.70) and a quadrupole contribution of 10%. These findings are consistent with models of nearby, anisotropic cosmic sources, such as those located in the Galactic Center or the Magellanic Clouds.

The concept of a zinbieli algebra arises from examining zinbiel algebras within a specific variety where all nonabelian components are solvable. The investigation into these structures in arbitrary Lie algebras begins by considering them as the centralizer of an element inside an associative algebra equipped with a modified multiplication rule. The primary result of this work establishes that any zinbieli algebra is itself solvable.

Fluctuations in the transverse flow angle and transverse flow velocity have been investigated in central Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 5.02 TeV at the LHC, utilizing proton-to-pion, proton-to-proton, and pion-to-pion transverse mass correlations. The analysis employs a blast-wave model to extract fluctuations in the average transverse flow angle ($\langle\psi\rangle$) and transverse flow velocity ($\gamma_T$) as functions of the transverse momentum ($p_T$). These fluctuations are found to be substantial for $p_T >$ 1.0 GeV/c, with the magnitude of $\langle\psi\rangle$ fluctuations decreasing as $p_T$ increases. The observed $\gamma_T$ fluctuations are attributed to fluctuations in the initial energy density distribution, and the results are compared against theoretical predictions from the IP-Glasma and EPOS models.

This study introduces a framework for addressing inconsistencies in relational tables containing null values and functional dependencies (FDs). We define a specific class of FDs and demonstrate that, for this class, a sound and complete algorithm exists to determine whether a table violates any given dependency. Our approach relies on a semantic interpretation of FDs where nulls are treated as representing an unknown set of values. We also examine the impact of alternative semantic definitions on the problem's complexity and present a polynomial-time solution for the scenario where nulls denote a known set of values.

This paper introduces a new class of models known as time-dependent Poisson regressions, which allow regression coefficients to evolve according to various linear time series frameworks, including both univariate and multivariate autoregressive structures. We formally define these models, establish their theoretical properties, and propose an efficient computational algorithm for analysis. To illustrate their practical application, we analyze historical data from the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) trading volume. Additionally, we develop and apply this novel approach to enhance the modeling of count data in the context of terrorism attacks in the Middle East.

Neural implicit representations have recently emerged as a leading approach for 3D scene and object reconstruction, yet their current methods often lack full rotational and translational invariance. This deficiency can result in inconsistent implicit surfaces and unreliable performance in downstream applications such as neural rendering and 3D scene assembly. To address this, we introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDF), a novel framework that integrates object-level semantic information with high-frequency local geometric details. NNDs achieve this by combining a global object embedding with a set of location-dependent neural descriptors. We validate the effectiveness of Neural Descriptor Fields through several key contributions: first, we demonstrate that object-level semantics significantly enhance reconstruction quality, particularly in completing incomplete scans; second, we introduce a new dataset comprising both raw and processed multi-view images for ten distinct objects; and third, we establish new state-of-the-art results on the ShapeNetComplete benchmark using only unregistered, unaligned, and incomplete views.

We have investigated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity within the three-dimensional classic O(N) universality classes using Monte Carlo simulations. By analyzing the singular point at $\theta_{MLE}$ through multiple estimators, we establish that $\theta_{MLE} = -1.0192(2)$ for the O(2) model and $\theta_{MLE} = -1.0188(2)$ for the O(3) model. These findings support the hypothesis that the singular position resides at the universal value $\theta_{MLE} = -\cos(\pi/5)$ across all $N \geq 4$ classes, which is consistent with our derived prediction of $\theta_{MLE} = -1.01888(1)$ for the O(4) model.

We establish a novel form of the Gaussian Sudakov-Fernique inequality, referred to as "post-AMP," which applies to random matrices where the AMP algorithm converges. This result serves as a foundational element in proving the "local curvature of TAP free energy," a concept previously introduced by the authors under an alternative name. The demonstration of this local curvature constitutes a significant advancement in the analysis of high-dimensional statistical inference problems.

This study introduces a novel technique for monitoring aerosol optical depth (AOD) by analyzing the light curves of stars recorded via stellar photometry. The methodology involves training a deep neural network to model the intrinsic variability of stars, allowing for the detection of atmospheric signals in the residuals between observed and predicted light curves. Validated against ground-based AOD measurements from a sun photometer and satellite-derived AOD data, this approach demonstrates high accuracy. Its capability to monitor AOD continuously from dawn to dusk, with a temporal resolution of approximately one minute, offers a significant leap forward in both the frequency and duration of observations compared to conventional methods.

Human pose estimation is a fundamental computer vision task that has been widely explored. While most existing methods rely on 2D to 3D pose correspondence to achieve high accuracy, they often struggle with robustness in real-world scenarios. This paper introduces a novel approach that integrates projection clustering with correspondence learning to address these limitations. First, we extract 2D keypoints from multiple views of the target pose using a detector trained on synthetic data. Next, we perform clustering on these keypoints to generate a set of 3D candidate poses. Finally, we refine the most probable candidates by refining the 2D to 3D correspondences. Experiments conducted on the Human3.6M and NTU-RGBD datasets demonstrate that this method significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques.

UGraphLasso is a Python library designed to solve the Universal Graphical Lasso problem, extending the standard method to accommodate various regularization terms and constraints. This framework enables the computation of precise maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimates for numerous Bayesian network inference tasks, which typically involve specific priors and structural constraints. UGraphLasso operates with broad compatibility, functioning seamlessly within existing codebases and supporting diverse data types, including complex, sparse, and complex-number matrices. The package leverages efficient C++ algorithms via the Python interface, ensuring robust and high-performance execution.

Molecular simulations are constrained by the astronomical dimensionality of configurational space, which hampers efficient sampling. While the Langevin dynamics method offers a robust solution for navigating this vast landscape, it often converges too slowly due to the high friction required to dampen momentum. This study introduces a novel integrator for Langevin dynamics that accelerates convergence by incorporating a harmonic positional restraint to guide system evolution toward target regions. We validate the approach's efficacy and superior performance through applications to both small- and large-scale systems.

This paper introduces a novel framework for assessing node centrality in multilayer networks that accounts for the interdependence of importance scores across different layers. This approach addresses a significant gap in existing research, which has largely overlooked how such correlations influence eigenvector centrality in multilayer structures. We formulate a general model describing these cross-layer dependencies and apply it specifically to the eigenvector centrality algorithm. Our analysis demonstrates that when node importance is highly transferable between layers, the centrality of a node in any given layer is predominantly determined by the aggregate centrality of that node across the entire network. Furthermore, we establish an efficient iterative procedure to compute these centrality measures. The proposed framework offers significant advantages for real-world applications, including the evaluation of node significance in complex multilayer systems such as social media platforms and the ranking of entities in multilayered search engines.

This paper presents the derivation of Dirac's equation within Riemann–Cartan (R-C) space-time, incorporating both spin and torsion. It is demonstrated that the inclusion of torsion renders the R-C Dirac equation mathematically equivalent to the standard Dirac equation in Minkowski space. Furthermore, it is shown that the solutions to the C-Dirac equation in C-Minkowski space are also solutions to the corresponding C-Dirac equation in C-R-Minkowski space. Finally, it is suggested that the equivalence between the C-Dirac equation in C-R space-time and the standard C-Dirac equation in C-R space-time may be interpreted as a form of "Dirac's Holographic Principle."

This study investigates the surface-sealing effectiveness of spheres entering water at high velocities, specifically within the intermediate speed range where $Fr_d$ is between 0.1 and 10 (with $Fr_d$ representing the diameter Froude number). This regime is critical because it marks the transition from an air-entraining impact to a sealed, air-excluding event. The research focuses on how key parameters—entry velocity, sphere surface roughness, and material density—influence sealing performance. Experiments were conducted across a broad spectrum of diameter Froude numbers ($Fr_d$) and Reynolds numbers ($Re_d$), covering $0.1 < Fr_d < 10$, $10^3 < Re_d < 10^6$, and a velocity span of $2 < U_0 < 100$ m/s. The data collected includes entry velocity, surface roughness, sphere material density, and the resulting sealing performance. The findings indicate that surface roughness and material density significantly affect sealing outcomes, whereas the initial entry velocity has a negligible impact. Furthermore, the study establishes a new, unified correlation for sealing performance that applies across the entire intermediate speed regime.

We examine global symmetry breaking within the generalized structure of discrete gauge groups in Type IIB supergravity, focusing on the interplay between $\theta$-terms and the Chern-Simons term. Our analysis reveals that specific combinations of these terms transform as a doublet under an emergent global $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ symmetry, which acts as a subgroup of the $E_{7(7})$ duality group associated with $SL(2)$ rotations of the complexified axio-dilaton. This $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ invariance is spontaneously broken by a vacuum expectation value of a scalar field residing in a vector multiplet, thereby reducing the global $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ symmetry to a discrete $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. This $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry corresponds to electric-magnetic duality, which interchanges the $\theta$-term and the Chern-Simons term. Consequently, the spontaneous breaking of global $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ symmetry necessitates the presence of generalized $\theta$-terms in the vacuum. We further demonstrate that this mechanism of generalized $\theta$-term generation applies equally to global symmetries emerging in $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauged supergravity.

The magnetic and orbital ordering of CuFe$_2$S$_3$ (cubanite) is investigated through temperature-dependent optical spectroscopy and theoretical modeling. Analysis of the reflectance spectra reveals distinct changes in the optical response, which are interpreted as evidence for magnetic ordering occurring at approximately 100 K and a reorganization of the Fe $3d$ orbitals near 200 K. These findings indicate that orbital-selective behavior characterizes the electronic structure of cubanite.

We investigate the coherent control of a dark exciton artificial atom, where a circularly polarized laser tunes transitions between a ground state and a superposition of bright and dark excitons. Our analysis reveals that fluctuations in Rabi oscillation amplitudes arise from spontaneous emission of virtual photons, a mechanism that persists even when external magnetic fields are absent. Furthermore, we demonstrate that adjusting this magnetic field allows for the tuning of Rabi fluctuations, which can reach magnitudes exceeding 10%. These findings suggest that such a system is well-suited for exploring quantum coherence in artificial atoms and could serve as a sensitive probe for spontaneous emission.

"Dirac fermions, characterized by linear dispersion relations at specific points in the first Brillouin zone, are typically found in graphene and other carbon allotropes. Although various mechanisms like spin-orbit coupling, magnetic fields, and structural distortions can open gaps at Dirac points, these structures remain highly sensitive to external perturbations. This study demonstrates that a two-dimensional non-symmorphic wallpaper network lattice (specifically p2mg) can host multiple Dirac points. The positions of these points are adjusted by varying the lattice's internal parameters. Unlike the high-symmetry locations of Dirac points in conventional graphene, those in this non-symmorphic wallpaper network reside at low-symmetry k-vectors. Furthermore, the electronic bands near these points exhibit a distinctive non-symmorphic 'folded' geometry. The paper examines the origins of these Dirac points and analyzes how the lattice's tunability influences their stability and dispersion."

We introduce a novel method for creating quantum-optical coherent states by utilizing single-photon catalysis. In this approach, a coherent state interacts with a single-photon Fock state via a nonlinear optical interaction, allowing the photon to be absorbed and the state to emerge as a new coherent state with a distinct phase. We demonstrate that this phase shift, known as the single-photon catalyzed coherent phase, can be tuned by adjusting the amplitude of the initial coherent state. Furthermore, we examine the relationship between this generated phase and the single-photon assisted Rabi flopping, highlighting the role of quantum interference in the process.

This work explores the application of bivectors within the General Relativity framework using the Newman-Penrose formalism. We demonstrate how the real and imaginary components of the Weyl tensor's scalar coefficients emerge through the Bivectors of complex self-dual and anti-self-dual bivectors. Furthermore, we illustrate how the real-valued parts of the Maxwell tensor's scalar coefficients are derived via Bivectors applied to the electromagnetic field tensor.

Inferring a molecule's structure from its properties is a critical task in computational chemistry and drug discovery. This study introduces a novel method for identifying molecular structures that align with specific property values by modeling the relationship between molecular fingerprints and properties using linear regression. We frame this structure-inference challenge as an integer programming problem, which we solve via column generation. Column generation is adapted here to resolve the complex sub-problems arising in structure validity checks. We evaluate our approach against existing methods on two public datasets: the QM9 collection of small organic molecules and a subset of the US Patent Office's repository containing millions of molecules. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques in both accuracy and execution speed.

Automatic segmentation of esophageal tumors is a critical task for diagnosing and treating diseases such as esophageal cancer. However, existing deep learning segmentation methods often underperform due to the small size of tumors in medical images, which hinders their widespread adoption. To address these limitations, we propose DDAUnet, a novel framework built on the U-Net architecture that integrates dilated convolutions and dense connections. This design enhances the model's ability to capture fine-grained details and extract high-level features, thereby improving segmentation accuracy. Furthermore, we introduce a novel loss function designed to mitigate class imbalance caused by the scarcity of tumor pixels. Evaluated on the public KTT dataset, our approach demonstrates superior performance compared to other state-of-the-art methods, with Dice similarity coefficients ranging from 0.80 to 0.90.

Code mixing, a phenomenon where two or more languages are interwoven within a single sentence, is prevalent in multilingual societies. This study investigates the difficulties and influences affecting natural language processing (NLP) tasks for code-mixed text. We examine three specific areas: the scarcity of annotated datasets, the hurdles posed by language variability, and the obstacles related to morphological complexity. Furthermore, we present empirical findings from experiments utilizing code-switched Hindi-English text for both named entity recognition and natural language inference. Our findings indicate that existing NLP models encounter significant challenges when applied to code-mixed scenarios.

Automatic image description models are typically assessed using human-generated references as a baseline, even though these are costly to obtain. This study investigates the necessity of such expensive data for evaluation. We introduce a method that trains evaluators to generate image captions using only the images themselves, and we demonstrate that descriptions from these machine-taught annotators perform comparably to those from human experts on standard image description tasks.

Tantalum oxide (Ta$_2$O$_5$) is a promising candidate for next-generation gate dielectrics in high-k technology. This study employs phonon calculations based on density functional theory to investigate the thermodynamic stability of its various polymorphs. We identified the $\gamma$-phase as the most stable structure at 0 K, a result that contradicts experimental observations where the $\alpha$-phase predominates under ambient conditions. To resolve this discrepancy, we applied Monte Carlo simulations to analyze the influence of entropy and defects. Our findings indicate that vibrational and defect entropies are insufficient to stabilize the $\alpha$-phase at room temperature, suggesting instead that configurational entropy plays a decisive role. Furthermore, we propose a novel defect mechanism involving oxygen vacancies that effectively explains the prevalence of the $\alpha$-phase in real-world scenarios. Finally, we present a revised phase diagram for Ta$_2$O$_5$ that incorporates these entropic contributions and the identified vacancy mechanism.

This study examines the role of the Big Geographic Shift (BigGS) in the dissemination of misinformation among Reddit users in the United States. We analyze a dataset of 1.5 billion comments from the r/news subreddit, which serves as the primary news hub for the English-speaking U.S. population. Our findings indicate that during the BigGS, misinformation spreads more rapidly and reaches a broader audience compared to other periods. Furthermore, we observe that while the BigGS significantly amplifies the spread of such content, it does not alter the inherent characteristics of the commenters themselves.

Human-robot interaction research increasingly emphasizes natural communication methods, including speech, to enhance collaborative efficiency. However, current studies predominantly examine linguistic content while often overlooking the acoustic characteristics of speech. This work investigates the acoustic traits of verbal instructions provided by human teachers to robots performing manipulation tasks. We collected a dataset comprising spoken demonstrations from multiple instructors, which were segmented into semantic units known as demonstration episodes. These episodes were categorized into three distinct groups based on their acoustic features. Our findings reveal that these features effectively differentiate between instructional segments, suggesting that acoustic properties carry meaningful information regarding task structure. Consequently, integrating such features can significantly improve the efficiency of robots in learning human-demonstrated manipulation skills.

We establish a new formula for the intracancy of diagonal minimal models by proving that $c$ conformal weight equals the negative of the accumulated time within the diagonal Cartan–Meyer Euler-Arnold system evolving from the initial diagonal Kac label configuration. This result generalizes earlier work by Sun and Yin, which defined the weight of irreducible representations of the affine algebra $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}(2)$ using the times of the classical $A_2$ rigid body motion.

Conversational agents are increasingly utilized to handle user interactions across a wide range of applications. However, the lack of comprehensive automated testing frameworks has hindered the ability to ensure the dependability of these systems. To address this gap, we introduce a novel framework designed for testing chatbots, which incorporates a specialized natural language generation module to execute automated test cases. We evaluated our solution by applying it to evaluate three distinct chatbots, demonstrating the framework's practical viability. Furthermore, we analyzed the results of these evaluations to offer actionable recommendations for enhancing the quality of conversational agents.

Recommendation systems are increasingly facing the challenge of sparsity, which hampers their ability to provide accurate suggestions. To address this, we introduce Multi-Domain Cooperative Recommendation (MDCR), a novel framework designed to boost recommendation performance by integrating information across various domains. Central to our approach is Enhanced Comprehensive Aspect Preference Learning (ECAPL), a method that identifies and incorporates multiple user preference signals. These signals include domain-specific preferences derived from explicit ratings, general preferences inferred from interactions in other domains, and collaborative signals from users sharing similar profiles. By synthesizing these diverse sources of information, ECAPL constructs a robust representation of user preferences that significantly improves the system's capability to handle sparse data. Comprehensive experiments conducted on real-world datasets demonstrate that our proposed framework consistently outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

Natural conic equations are defined by a convex function $f$ and a concave function $g$ over a domain $\Omega$, seeking solutions within the region where $f(x) \leq 1$ and $g(x) \leq 1$. This paper introduces a new algorithm utilizing Hypatia.jl to resolve such equations, relying on a trust-region framework that employs a self-concordant barrier derived from $f$ alongside a first-order approximation of $g$. We establish the algorithm's convergence to an $\epsilon$-approximate stationary point with a computational complexity of $O(\log^3(1/\epsilon))$. Furthermore, we propose a novel class of equations applicable to domain randomization in robotics, demonstrating how our method accelerates sampling compared to existing approaches. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/ahenderson/Hypatia.

Accurate quality assurance is essential for ensuring the reliability of MRI data in both clinical and research environments. We introduce a deep learning framework designed to automate quality assurance for brain MRI data, which we trained and assessed on a large, diverse collection of MRI scans sourced from various research studies and clinical settings. Our research highlights that generalizing this framework across such heterogeneous datasets constitutes a complex task driven by multiple factors. We systematically investigate these influences—specifically batch size, training duration, and data ordering—and develop strategies to enhance the model's performance. Additionally, we examine the framework's behavior regarding different input modalities, including single-channel, multi-channel, and concatenated inputs. Our findings reveal that generalization on this multifaceted task is significantly improved by optimizing these hyperparameters, training dynamics, and data presentation methods.

This study introduces a Multi-Agent Optimization (MAO) framework designed to assess the impact of privately owned electric vehicles (POEVs) on the resilience of distribution networks facing disruptions. The approach models the network as a multi-agent system where each agent represents a distinct stakeholder—utility companies, network operators, and private EV drivers—interacting through a Stackelberg game. Utility companies and operators act as leaders, optimizing their strategies to maximize profit and network reliability, respectively, while private drivers act as followers, aiming to minimize travel expenses. To incorporate the stochastic nature of EV charging, a Markov Decision Process (MDP) is employed to determine optimal charging policies for private agents. Furthermore, the research evaluates various disruption scenarios, including complete line outages, partial capacity reductions, and communication failures, to analyze how POEVs influence system robustness. Key contributions include modeling stakeholder interactions via a Stackelberg game, developing an MDP for EV charging behavior under uncertainty, and investigating the effects of infrastructure failures on network performance. The findings reveal that private EVs can significantly degrade network resilience, particularly when charging demand is high and outage magnitudes are severe.

This study introduces a multi-agent Recurrent Meeting (MARUM) framework designed to facilitate repeated interactions among autonomous agents. Unlike existing methods that rely on rigid, pre-programmed schedules, MARUM utilizes motivation derived from actual travel experiences to naturally foster recurring encounters. Within this system, agents establish a shared memory of past trips and employ a reinforcement learning strategy to select motivations for future meetings. The validity of this approach is demonstrated through simulations involving various agent types, which reveal that the proposed framework successfully facilitates repeated meetings.

This study employs the full-potential linearized augmented plane-wave method within the framework of density functional theory to examine the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn$_3$, CmSn$_3$, and Gd$_x$Cm$_x$Sn$_{1-x}$ (where $x = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75$) in both non-magnetic and various magnetic configurations. Our findings reveal that GdSn$_3$ and CmSn$_3$ exhibit antiferromagnetic ground states, with GdSn$_3$ adopting the $\Gamma_2$ representation and CmSn$_3$ adopting the $\Gamma_4$ representation. Furthermore, our results indicate that Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_{1-x}$ is a topological crystalline antiferromagnet. The study also analyzes the effects of lattice constant variations and different magnetic configurations on the electronic and magnetic properties of these compounds.

This study examines the predictions for additional baryons and mesons, a subject of growing interest in high-energy physics. We analyze the underlying theoretical frameworks, including the parton model, perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD), and the Lund string model. Furthermore, we explore the application of these concepts in diverse high-energy environments, such as proton-proton collisions, heavy ion collisions, and cosmic ray events.

We analyze the 10,080 Type Ia supernovae in the Pantheon dataset to investigate weak gravitational lensing effects. By examining the distribution of apparent magnitudes and redshifts, we derive a mean weak lensing convergence of $\langle\kappa\rangle = 0.0123 \pm 0.0006$, consistent with expectations from large-scale structure formation. This study represents the most extensive analysis of weak lensing applied to Type Ia supernovae to date.

T junctions are fundamental components in silicon-based photonic integrated circuits, yet developing accurate and efficient mathematical models for their behavior remains a significant challenge. This study introduces a rigorous 3D vectorial theory for T junctions fabricated in silicon-on-insulator technology. The model's predictions for transmission and reflection coefficients are validated against both full-wave numerical simulations and experimental data. Furthermore, the theoretical framework is applied to analyze the complex scattering dynamics within photonic-T networks.

Object detection algorithms have advanced significantly, yet their performance often varies depending on the specific scene. This study introduces a systematic approach to evaluate the criticality of contextual information for object detectors. We present a novel framework utilizing a synthetic object database where target instances are placed in diverse real-world contexts. By training and assessing deep object detectors on this dataset, we observe that these models struggle to locate objects against unfamiliar backgrounds. Furthermore, our experiments reveal that detectors achieve higher accuracy when provided with objects from non-trivial poses and complex scenes. Ultimately, this work offers a robust benchmark for evaluating deep object detectors under challenging contextual conditions.

This study investigates the existence of multiple solutions for a Kirchhoff-type elliptic system in $\mathbb{R}^2$ governed by critical growth at the exceptional Trudinger-Moser level. By applying the theory of genus and the theory of linking within a framework of critical geometry, we establish that the set of solutions containing both ground state and non-ground state elements is infinite.

This paper examines concentration inequalities for the sum of binary random variables exhibiting specific types of negative correlations. We analyze two distinct correlation frameworks: (i) the negative quadrant dependence (NQD) of pairs, and (i) the negative orthant dependence (NOD) of k-tuples where k≥2. Under these assumptions, we derive Hoeffding-type and Bernstein-type inequalities. Furthermore, we explore the connection between NQD and NQD structures.

A symplectic conversion is defined as a smooth map that simultaneously functions as a Lagrangian immersion and a symplectic embedding. This paper investigates the fundamental properties of such conversions, demonstrating that both the map and its inverse are automatically smooth. We further explore the relationship between symplectic conversions and symplectic isomorphisms, establishing a criterion for when a map qualifies as a symplectic isomorphism based on these conversions.

Deceased donor kidney transplantation remains constrained by a shortage of available organs, prompting the use of an acceptance algorithm that matches only a subset of compatible offers. While existing methods prioritize maximizing the growth of existing transplant cycles within the matching framework, they often overlook the potential of "unmatched" kidneys—those compatible with no currently transplanted recipient. This study investigates the strategic value of prioritizing these unmatched kidneys within the standard matching protocol. We introduce a hierarchical algorithm that first guarantees the integration of all unmatched compatible kidneys and subsequently optimizes cycle growth among remaining matches. Our analysis of historical data from 2014 to 2018 demonstrates that this "Unmatched-First" approach significantly boosts the total number of transplants compared to the standard strategy, with a 99% statistical certainty.

This study investigates whether word embedding models capture the sentiment polarity definitions established by the Loughran-McDonald (LM) dictionary. We evaluate prominent embeddings, including Word2Vec, GloVe, and fastText, against the specific financial domain nuances outlined in the LM dictionary. Our analysis reveals that while these embeddings successfully mirror the directional polarity of terms (distinguishing positive from negative), they often fail to accurately represent the intensity of those emotions. Furthermore, the study highlights notable variations in how different embedding algorithms perform when tasked with this form of semantic understanding.

This study extends the work of Li et al. (IEEE J. Sel. Areas Commun., 2020) by developing optimal wideband waveforming strategies for integrated data and energy transmission in SISO- and MISO-OFDM systems. We formulate distinct optimization problems tailored to each configuration and derive closed-loop solutions using convex optimization techniques. Numerical results confirm that these proposed waveform outperforms conventional orthogonal methods in both data rates and energy delivery capabilities.

This study introduces a level-set embedded boundary technique designed to simulate solidification and melting processes involving complex, evolving interfaces. The method integrates an efficient reinitialization strategy with an embedded boundary framework to accurately model intricate interface dynamics. During the solution of the temperature field, a moving mesh transformation converts the problem into one on a fixed computational domain, with interface conditions incorporated as additional constraints within the discrete system. This approach allows interface features to be resolved using a grid resolution independent of the mesh density. The proposed method is validated through numerical experiments that demonstrate its accuracy and effectiveness when applied to solidification and melting scenarios characterized by complex interface behaviors.

Equilibria represent a fundamental concept in economics, yet their utility is often hindered by the lack of interpretability in the strategies that constitute them. Addressing this, we introduce a framework for learning correlated equilibria in $n$-player games where each agent belongs to a specific group with limited size $k$. Within this setup, every player must select a strategy based solely on a local policy dependent on at most $k$ dimensions. We establish an algorithm that learns an $\epsilon$-equilibrium satisfying these constraints using $O(\frac{\text{poly}(n)}{\epsilon^2}\log(n)\cdot \max_i \frac{|\mathcal{A}_i|}{\delta^2})$ samples, where $|\mathcal{A}_i|$ denotes the cardinality of player $i$'s action space. Furthermore, we propose a method to train shallow neural networks to serve as these local policies. We validate our approach through experiments in a competitive three-player setting, demonstrating that our algorithm successfully learns equilibria explainable via such networks.

This study examines epidemic dynamics within a dynamic network where infection transmission can trigger structural changes. We introduce a rewiring mechanism: upon acquiring an infection, a healthy individual may sever a link connected to a currently uninfected neighbor and establish a new connection elsewhere in the network. This behavior models a preventive response to potential disease introduction. We demonstrate that the epidemic's final size adheres to a branching process and derive conditions ensuring its convergence. Furthermore, we establish a sharp threshold separating two distinct regimes—an outbreak affecting a significant portion of the population versus one that remains limited. We also analyze the expected number of infections under both static and evolving network conditions. Finally, we provide numerical simulations that illustrate how the rewiring rate influences the final epidemic magnitude.

This work introduces a general Bayesian framework designed to incorporate prior knowledge into Parton Distribution Function (PDF) fitting. This approach addresses the issue of non-uniqueness in fitting, allowing for the specification of various types of prior information. We demonstrate the utility of this theory by fitting the NNPDF3.0 collaboration's data, successfully integrating recent measurements of the $Z$-boson rapidity from the CMS and LHCb experiments at the LHC. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of including these new datasets on the resulting PDFs and their associated uncertainties.

In the domain of reinforcement learning, experience replay serves as a foundational technique for enhancing sample efficiency. However, the inherent variance within bootstrapped updates often degrades the learning of policies that are already well-trained. To address this, we introduce Variance Diminution Experience Replay (VD-ER), a strategy designed to minimize the variance of sampled transitions drawn from the replay buffer. We provide a theoretical analysis demonstrating that variance reduction in the offline dataset leads to diminished variance in the resulting policy, thereby accelerating convergence. Furthermore, we introduce an importance sampling-based method to retrieve data from the buffer with reduced stochasticity. Our experimental results across various environments demonstrate that VD-ER significantly outperforms existing approaches in both policy convergence speed and overall performance.

Existing dialogue generation models often struggle with diversity and naturalness because current branching testbeds rely on manually created, linear child nodes that limit the variety of subsequent turns. To overcome these limitations, we introduce MultiTalk, a new dialogue testing framework featuring highly branched structures. By automatically generating multiple diverse responses for every single input sentence, our method eliminates the need for manual content creation. We validate our approach using the standard MultiWOZ dataset, which our results show successfully produces a six-branch dialogue tree originating from any given seed. Furthermore, experiments indicate that top-large language models (LLMs) utilizing MultiTalk generate dialogues that are both more varied and more natural compared to those generated using the traditional FRED testbed.

We introduce a new class of modified gravity models defined by conformal couplings between curvature and matter, designed specifically for efficient emulation via full $N$-body simulations. These models are formulated to be free of ghosts and Laplacian instabilities, with specific choices of the coupling function enabling the reproduction of both $\Lambda$CDM and $\sim$CDM dynamics. We implement an efficient, axisymmetric, periodic boundary condition scheme that allows these models to run approximately three times faster than standard Particle-Mesh methods. This enhanced speed facilitates the generation of massive emulators, which we demonstrate using a pilot run containing $2\times 2\times 2$ $2048^3$ dark matter particles in a $1\,\text{Gpc}/h$ periodic box. Current efforts are underway to scale these calculations to even larger volumes and particle counts.

We examine the conditional joint distributions of several chordal Loewner trajectories, driven by log-gas processes in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}$ and conditioned on $\gamma_k(1) = 0$ for $k \neq 1$. By leveraging the correlation functions of classical orthogonal polynomials, we establish that these random trajectories generate a Gaussian free field on $\mathbb{H}$ coupled with multiple SLEs driven by independent log-gas processes. This extends previous results by Sheffield and Werner, which assumed drivers were independent of one another.

WorkingWiki functions as an open-source, free extension of MediaWiki specifically tailored for research teams. It builds upon the established capabilities of MediaWiki by introducing specialized features designed to enhance academic teamwork. Currently in its second beta stage, WorkingWiki aims to streamline the research process through robust tools for project management, task assignment, and the organization of collaborative writing efforts.

This study investigates the reaction of a turbulent jet flame to acoustic forcing within a linearized framework, employing an active flame model. The analysis utilizes a first-order acoustic approximation to treat the jet flow, while the flame itself is modeled as a linearized Dirac delta function source term in the momentum equations. The linearization process involves expanding the flow and flame characteristics around a base state, which is determined via Large Eddy Simulation (LES) under ambient conditions. The base state is decomposed into a mean component and a turbulent fluctuation, with the latter treated statistically. The mean flow is derived from LES data, whereas the turbulent fluctuations are closed using the dynamic Smagorinsky model. The LES results indicate that the mean flow exhibits significant non-Gaussianity and non-axisymmetry, with the latter attributed to the swirled inlet conditions. The study further examines the linearization of the flame transfer function, which relates inlet velocity fluctuations to heat release rate fluctuations. This function is decomposed into a mean part and a turbulent component, with the latter modeled as a Gaussian process possessing a specific covariance structure inferred from LES data. The mean velocity fluctuation is found to be negligible compared to the mean, whereas the turbulent velocity fluctuation is comparable in magnitude to the mean. The paper also explores the impact of forcing on the jet, revealing that forcing at the most energetic natural frequency of the jet results in the largest heat release response. We investigate the impact of interactions between neutrinos and ultralight dark matter (ULDM) on neutrinoless double beta decay ($0
u eta eta$) and cosmological evolution. We derive a revised expression for the $0
u eta eta$ half-life that incorporates ULDM fluctuations and demonstrate that these variations can enhance decay rates by up to 100%, thereby tightening constraints on ULDM models. Furthermore, we analyze ULDM effects on neutrino encounters during matter-radiation and matter-matter encounters within cosmology, finding that ULDM can alter the neutrino free-streaming epoch and matter radiation equality by approximately 10%. These findings suggest that combining ULDM-specific $0
u eta eta$ data with precision cosmological observations offers a robust strategy for constraining ULDM parameters.

This work introduces a nonlocal gravity framework built upon a covariant constitutive approach, designed to integrate into general relativity by treating the gravitational field tensor as a function of the curvature tensor. The framework establishes a clear distinction between the kinematic and dynamic aspects of gravity, allowing for a unique decomposition of the Einstein-Hilbert action into irreducible components. This separation facilitates the derivation of field equations and their corresponding inverse forms, which are essential for constructing specific constitutive relations. The paper investigates both local and global nonlocal models, deriving the specific constitutive laws required to generate prescribed dynamics. Finally, the study applies this framework to cosmology and black hole scenarios, demonstrating how the proposed nonlocal geometry can be empirically validated.

This study investigates the relationship between genome-wide association (GWA) results and functional genomics for eight human traits, specifically focusing on schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and autism. We evaluate various genomic annotations, including chromatin states, transcription factor binding sites, and gene expression data, to assess their ability to identify GWA loci. Furthermore, we explore the impact of integrating multiple annotations and test different statistical methodologies. Our analysis reveals that the combination of annotations derived from the ENCODE project and FANTOM5 significantly enhances the identification of GWA loci associated with neuropsychiatric disorders. Additionally, we observed that the efficacy of specific annotations varies depending on the trait examined. Finally, we demonstrate that integrating annotations into GWA analysis yields more consistent results compared to other common sources of biological information.

The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) primarily aims to investigate the properties of the newly discovered Higgs boson and search for physics beyond the Standard Model. However, the high-energy proton-proton collisions inevitably produce a diverse array of other processes, known as "minor" or "other" systems. These include proton-neutron, proton-ion, ion-ion, and various hadronic interactions. These systems offer unique opportunities to explore Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) in extreme conditions, such as quark-gluon plasma formation, exotic hadronic structures, and the nature of the early universe. This paper provides a comprehensive review of recent significant experimental findings from the ATLAS, CMS, ALICE, and LHCb detectors regarding these minor systems at the LHC.

We examine the recurrence intervals of transient X-ray binaries involving accreting neutron stars, utilizing data from 1,000 such systems observed for at least 20 years. Our analysis reveals a bimodal distribution in these intervals, characterized by peaks near 1 year and 10 years, with a distinct scarcity of systems having intermediate durations. This finding implies that transient events are likely triggered by intrinsic properties of the neutron stars themselves, rather than extrinsic factors such as accretion disk instability. Furthermore, we propose that the population of quiescent X-ray binaries in the Galactic Centre consists primarily of long-interval transients, thereby challenging models that attribute their invisibility to the disruption of companion stars by tidal forces.

This study introduces a novel momentum-dependent electron-phonon and spin-phonon interaction, which serves as a generalization of the conventional momentum-independent forms. We demonstrate that this new coupling generates a momentum transfer between electrons and the lattice, yielding a dynamical Higgs-like mode. This phenomenon is analyzed within the framework of the BCS theory of superconductivity and the Heisenberg model of magnetism. Our findings reveal that this electron-lattice coupling can significantly influence both magnetic and superconducting phase diagrams, as well as the associated critical temperatures and order parameters.

This study introduces a novel Natural Language Inference (NLI) task designed to enhance the representation of semantic diversity in human conversation. We posit that current dialogue models often fail to adequately capture this variety, a shortcoming that hampers their ability to generate natural and engaging exchanges. To address this, we propose an NLI-based dialogue framework where a "premise" utterance and a "hypothesis" utterance are drawn from the same conversation turn, with the goal of classifying their logical relationship. We have established a new dataset comprising 1.5 million instances from multi-turn English conversations, annotated with five distinct NLICategories: Entailment, Contradiction, Neutral, Unknown, and Other. Our analysis reveals that top-performing dialogue models currently underrepresent the "Other" category, which includes the most complex inference types. We evaluate our methodology using both standard and dialogue-specific metrics, demonstrating that incorporating this variety-focused task yields measurable improvements in conversational quality.

We simulated the structural evolution of rotating, self-gravitating, substellar bodies—encompassing brown dwarfs and giant planets—subject to radiative and convective energy transport, magnetic fields, and the Kelvin-Helmholtz contraction mechanism. These models explore mass-shedding limits across a range of initial conditions, specifically varying initial masses ($10^{-3}$ to $100\,M_{\odot}$), initial rotation rates, and initial entropies. The results indicate that rapid rotation significantly accelerates cooling and contraction compared to non-rotating objects. Furthermore, the time required to reach the mass-shedding limit decreases as initial mass increases, regardless of the specific initial state. The study also examines the impact of magnetic fields on the mass-shedding threshold, finding that while strong fields can inhibit contraction and delay the approach to this limit, they do not prevent it. Finally, we compared our numerical outputs with observational data regarding the mass and rotation characteristics of the ultra-low-mass stellar and planetary populations.

Amplitude analyses are extensively employed to investigate particle decay processes, with the integration of advanced machine learning techniques becoming increasingly prevalent. However, these methods often lack rigorous theoretical foundations and are highly dependent on specific implementations. This work introduces a theoretically sound framework for implementing experimental influences within such analyses, utilizing the method of analytic continuation to incorporate both detector response and background components. We demonstrate the application of this approach in the study of $D^0\to K^+\pi^-\pi^+\pi^-$, showing that it effectively models background and efficiency variations. Furthermore, we highlight that this method offers a more robust alternative to prevalent machine learning-based strategies.

A new model for gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) has been developed, featuring a relativistic jet with an energy distribution $dN/dE\propto E^{-p}$ that interacts with the interstellar medium (ISM). This approach eliminates the need for ad hoc assumptions regarding the jet's structure, magnetic fields, or the afterglow emission mechanism. Instead, the model derives the self-similar hydrodynamic solutions directly from the conservation of energy and momentum. The resulting framework successfully explains the temporal evolution of both afterglows and gamma-ray bursts across various scenarios, including external shocks within ISM, ISM-wintered interstellar medium (WSM), and circumstellar winds (CSM), as well as the internal shocks responsible for gamma-ray emission. Specifically, the time dependence of afterglow flux in the observer's frame is given by $F_{\nu} \propto t^{-(3-p)/2}$ for ISM and $F_{\nu} \propto t^{-(7-3p)/4}$ for CSM interactions. This "new generic model" offers a unified description of dynamical progressions observed in GRBs and their afterglows, providing a robust interpretation for phenomena such as those seen in GRB 030329, 990417, 991208, 000418, 000418, 00041

This paper investigates the bipartite vertex splitting problem within a graph $G=(V,E)$, where a subset $S \subseteq V$ forms a "known" part and the complement forms the "unknown" part. The objective is to determine the adjacencies between $S$ and the unknown vertices such that the resulting graph becomes bipartite. We establish an algorithm that solves this problem in time $O(|E|(1+|S|)^{k})$, where $k$ represents the solution's parameter. This result is significant because it transforms an NP-complete task into a class of problems solvable in fixed-parameter tractable time.

Bipedal robots are increasingly vital for executing complex tasks in unstructured environments, yet they face significant hurdles regarding efficiency and robustness. This paper introduces a thruster-augmented humanoid framework designed to overcome these challenges. We present a comprehensive modeling approach that incorporates both rigid-body and flexible dynamics, utilizing a robust nonlinear Model Predictive Control (MPC) strategy. This controller ensures continuous contact force regulation and trajectory tracking while accommodating the added degrees of freedom from thrusters and joint flexibility. Furthermore, we define a novel cost function specifically optimized to enhance locomotion efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that this method achieves stable walking with improved efficiency and greater resilience to disturbances and model inaccuracies.

This paper introduces the concept of a valued domain, defined as an integral domain $D$ equipped with a valuation-like residue map $\lambda: D \to D$. We demonstrate that if $D$ is a Noetherian domain of dimension at least two and $\lambda$ is a standard valuation map, then $D$ must be isomorphic to a polynomial ring $R[x]$ over a subring $R$ of positive characteristic $p$, where $R$ itself possesses a nontrivial valued field of fractions. Furthermore, we fully characterize all possible residue-like maps $\lambda$ for both valuation domains and discrete valuation domains $V$.

This paper introduces HyperDegrade, a novel technique for enhancing the confidentiality of data processed on the CPU. By deliberately slowing down processor clock speeds from gigahertz levels to megahertz levels, HyperDegrade disrupts side-channel attacks that rely on precise power consumption measurements and cache timing. Unlike existing methods, this approach operates without needing access to the specific target application, making it applicable in real-world scenarios. We evaluated HyperDegrade against prominent attacks, including those targeting the L1 cache, L2 cache, and the L1 data cache using both Pragma and Prime+Probe techniques. Our findings demonstrate that HyperDegrade effectively mitigates these threats, reducing the success rate of Pragma+Probe attacks by a factor of 100.

We introduce a new entangling operation applicable to both welded and classical links, with the resulting structures in each case forming groups that are isomorphic. This group isomorphism serves as a distinction between these new concepts and previous variants of links. We further analyze the relationship between the isomorphic groups generated from classical links and those produced by the new concept.

This paper demonstrates that the Fox-Hatcher loop, when evaluated within the context of the Alexander module associated with the trefoil knot's group, yields a non-trivial element within the abelianization of the free abelian group of rank 3. Consequently, this result establishes the existence of a Vassiliev knot invariant of finite order exactly 3 that applies specifically to the Fox-Hatcher loop.

This paper addresses the challenge of multi-task synchronization for a network of robots, where each agent must execute a specific task while maintaining alignment with peers. We formulate this as a non-cooperative, non-zero-sum, and non-coordinated game, wherein robots autonomously select their control laws to maximize individual performance metrics. The resulting Nash equilibrium is analyzed to determine the resulting synchronization accuracy. Furthermore, we introduce a novel multi-task synchronization protocol that ensures a Nash-equilibrium state with a bounded synchronization error. The proposed approach is validated through a simulation involving a group of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).

Federated learning (FL) enables multiple independent parties to collaboratively train machine learning models while preserving data privacy. Vertical federated learning (VFL) represents a key extension of FL, allowing parties to jointly perform tasks on disjoint, non-overlapping datasets based on specific entity attributes. Although VFL has gained significant traction in commercial applications, it remains vulnerable to privacy breaches by malicious participants. In this paper, we introduce practical attacks targeting VFL, focusing on a high-stakes scenario where a bank and a credit reporting agency collaborate to create a credit scoring model. In this context, the reporting agency acts as the adversary, aiming to reconstruct private client information from the bank's users. We evaluate the efficacy of our attacks in both simulated and real-world environments, demonstrating that a malicious reporting agency can successfully recover private information with a 90.01\% accuracy rate when employing a generative adversarial network (GAN).

Kernel methods are renowned for their efficacy in machine learning applications, yet they often require exponential computational costs concerning the input data dimensionality. To address this, recent innovations have employed random Fourier features to approximate kernels, enabling linear complexity with respect to dimensionality. However, these traditional approaches remain data-agnostic in their feature map generation, a limitation that restricts performance on high-dimensional inputs. This paper introduces a novel framework for kernel estimation via random Fourier features that is both data-dependent and precise. By leveraging the input dataset to construct feature maps, the proposed method achieves superior accuracy compared to existing techniques while maintaining linear complexity relative to dimensionality. Furthermore, we present an efficient algorithm for generating the specific feature maps required by this model. Extensive experiments across classification and regression tasks demonstrate that the data-driven kernel estimator consistently outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches in accuracy, with only a marginal increase in overall computation time.

This paper introduces a novel method called Cartesian Breakdown to establish embed the theorems regarding groups formed as direct, restricted, or wreathed products. Utilizing this framework, we derive new results covering abelian groups, specifically demonstrating that the symmetric group $S_n$ embeds into the $k$-fold restricted direct product of copies of $S_{\lceil n/2^k \rceil}$ for any $k \geq 1$. Additionally, we prove a theorem characterizing groups $G$ such that $S_n$ embeds in $G^N$, where $N$ is sufficiently large relative to $|G|$, and provide new embeddings for various non-abelian groups, including $A_n$, $PGL(d,p)$, and $PSL(d,p)$. Finally, we address wreathed products by proving that $S_n$ embeds in the $k$-fold restricted direct product of wreathed products of copies of $S_{\lceil n/2^k \rceil}$, and by showing that $S_n$ embeds in the $k$-fold unrestricted direct product of wreathed products of copies of $S_{\lceil n/2^k \rceil}$, where $k \geq 1$.

This paper investigates the dependence of the Möbius scalar curvature on Möbius equivalent structures for compact, codimension-one hypersurfaces within $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$ that are conforrmally flat. We establish that for any sufficiently smooth, compact, codimension-one, conformally flat hypersurface $M$ in $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$, there exists a unique Möbius transformation mapping $M$ into $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ such that the resulting Möbius scalar curvature attains its maximum value. Conversely, if $M$ yields a constant maximal Möbius scalar curvature under some Möbius transformation, it must correspond to a hyperquadric. Additionally, we explore the flexibility of the Möbius scalar curvature for compact, conformally flat, Möbius umbilical cases in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ and $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$, respectively. Specifically, we demonstrate that for compact, conformally flat, Möbius umbilical hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, the Möbius scalar curvature can assume any prescribed value $c \in \mathbb{R}$, whereas for those in $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$, the achievable values are restricted to $c \in (-\infty, -1] \cup [1

This study investigates the optimal allocation of power and time-circuit energy harvesting in wireless networks supporting both data transmission and simultaneous wireless information and power delivery (SWIP). We formulate a framework where a base station (BS) maximizes its own harvested energy by adjusting SWIP parameters, while ensuring a minimum data rate for an energy harvesting user (EHU). To achieve this, we establish a non-cooperative game where the EHUE acts as a player. We demonstrate that the resulting power allocation strategy constitutes a Nash Equilibrium (NE). Furthermore, we introduce an iterative algorithm to compute this equilibrium. Numerical simulations validate the proposed approach and confirm the existence of the NE.

This study examines the distribution of avalanche sizes within the Abelian sandpile model on infinite, finite-depth Cayley trees. By analyzing the exact distribution of both the magnitude of avalanches and their associated geometric characteristics, we demonstrate that these magnitudes follow a power law with an exponent of -1.0. This finding indicates a departure from the -1.0 power law typically observed in bulk self-organized critical systems and the -1.0 power law seen in infinite, bulk versions of this system. Furthermore, we investigate the spatial arrangement of these events, specifically the distribution of their sizes and shapes.

Gravitational wave detectors currently operate in a regime where their low-frequency sensitivity is constrained by radiation pressure noise. Enhancing this performance requires increasing the circulating power within the arm cavities; however, existing designs face a limitation: light cannot reach the end mirrors at high frequencies, thereby restricting power buildup. We propose a Sagnac-based architecture that overcomes this barrier by enabling light to strike the end mirrors with normal incidence across all frequencies. Our analysis indicates that this configuration could enhance high-frequency arm power by a factor of 100 compared to traditional Michelson interferometers, potentially improving low-frequency detector sensitivity by approximately 30%.

This paper presents a new random-access protocol designed for XL-MIMO systems, which utilizes a tree-based structure to ensure that the resource regions for valid user transmissions do not overlap. We define the conditions for non-interceptability and derive the associated probability of success. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of a "forbidden region" to model invalid resource regions and analyze its impact on the overall protocol performance. Based on these foundations, we propose a channel sounding-based random-access protocol. Our analytical results demonstrate that this proposed scheme achieves superior performance compared to existing methods.

This study investigates the formation of substructures in the dust continuum within disks affected by vertical shear instability (VSI), aiming to enhance observational support for the VSI mechanism. We employ the VSI framework to simulate the vertical structure of disks, utilizing the vertical hydrostatic approximation to model gas pressure responses to vertical forces. Our simulations track the evolution of gas surface density and midplane temperature under varying disk parameters, including mass, radius, and the Toomre $Q$ parameter. We then apply these results to predict observable features in dust emission, specifically examining the impact of VSI-driven density and thermal variations on the vertical distribution of dust grains. Our analysis indicates that VSI activity generates prominent gaps in dust continuum emission, accompanied by distinct inner and outer rims. These predicted structures align with recent observations of gaps in protoplanetary disks, offering strong evidence for the presence of VSI in these systems.

We investigate the "Big Apple" phenomenon, in which a carbon-12 nucleus fuses with a neon-20 nucleus to yield an excited oxygen-16 nucleus that fragments back into carbon-12 and neon-20. Utilizing the relativistic mean-field model, we demonstrate that this outcome arises from a pronounced peak in the binding energy per nucleon of oxygen-16, contrasting with the well-known magic stability of neighboring neon-20 and carbon-12. We further explore the implications of this effect on astrophysical processes and the synthesis of heavier elements, specifically analyzing the equation of state for neutron stars and the dynamics of supernovae.

This study introduces a frequency-tunable, frequency-resilient two-mode controlled-Mølmer-Sørensen (cMS) gate for trapped-ion systems, utilizing frequency contributions from multiple motional modes. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on a single mode, this method employs a two-mode cMS operation, where both the target qubit and an auxiliary qubit participate in the gate dynamics. By leveraging the auxiliary qubit, the protocol ensures that the entangling interaction remains largely insensitive to variations in trap frequencies. We demonstrate that this frequency-stabilized two-mode cMS gate achieves high fidelity even under significant frequency uncertainties, with minimal additional experimental overhead. Furthermore, we extend this concept to create a scalable, frequency-stable multi-qubit cMS gate. Numerical simulations indicate that this extended multi-qubit version maintains robust performance and high accuracy despite substantial frequency fluctuations.

We present a theoretical model of a highly tunable, strongly correlated Dirac metal featuring a robust, temperature-independent linear specific heat coefficient. This system is realized within a Kagome lattice of heavy p-orbitals, where a robust massless Dirac cone coexists with a flat band. The resulting material exhibits exceptional properties, including a linear specific heat dependence on temperature, a unique magnetic susceptibility profile, and a Hall effect that mirrors the signature of a single Dirac fermion despite the presence of multiple bands.

Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs), predicted by various Beyond Standard Model frameworks, could explain neutrino oscillations and other phenomena. This study estimates the reach of the CERN NA62 experiment for HLNs with masses below 4 GeV/c², produced via three-body decays of charged kaons ($K^+ \to \pi^0 e^+ N$). We project that the upgraded $\mu$-filter version of the NA62 apparatus can probe HNLs with electron mixing squared ($|U_{eN}|^2$) as low as $10^{-8}$ across the mass spectrum from 0 to 4 GeV/c².

Although neural language models have largely displaced traditional $n$-gram approaches for generating text, these neural methods often underperform $n$-grams on tasks requiring high precision. This paper argues that the underperformance stems not from the inherent flaws of $n$-grams, but from the inability of current neural architectures to effectively integrate them. We introduce a novel $n$-gram language model (NGM) that trains independently and functions as a distinct module within the neural pipeline. By treating NGM as a specialized task, we demonstrate through experiments that it significantly boosts the performance of various text generation neural networks when added to their training regimen. Furthermore, we show that combining NGM with a carefully selected subset of neural components yields superior results compared to using either approach alone.

We introduce a robust framework for 3D dense face alignment and reconstruction that simultaneously addresses two core challenges: accurately locating facial landmarks on unseen faces and generating dense 3D models that match specific individuals. To tackle these issues, we propose a Self-Aligned Dual Face Regression Network (SADRNet). This model integrates a shape prior generator, which creates a comprehensive 3D dense facial atlas, with a dual regression mechanism designed to locate landmarks on both visible and occluded portions of faces. The resulting 3D reconstruction is derived by combining the generated facial atlas with the localized landmarks. We evaluate our approach on three public datasets, demonstrating that SADRNet surpasses current state-of-the-art methods in both face landmark detection and 3D reconstruction tasks.

This study investigates the impact of a specific ultra-relativistic breakdown of the inflaton field on early cosmic evolution. By modeling the field as a massless, linearly coupled system within the $\alpha$-attractor inflation framework, we demonstrate that such perturbations trigger a phase transition in the radiation-dominated era, resulting in the generation of primordial black holes (PBHs). We further analyze PBH mass functions across various $\alpha$-attractor parameters, highlighting a correlation between the onset of PBH production and the amplitude of primordial curvature fluctuations. Additionally, we explore the potential for these events to generate gravitational waves and assess observational signatures of PBHs in the current epoch. Our findings indicate that PBH production becomes viable when the PBH mass falls below approximately $10^{-10}~\text{M}_{\odot}$, a threshold contingent upon the specific choice of $\alpha$. Consequently, this scenario offers a novel mechanism for PBH genesis that could potentially be detected through gravitational wave observations.

We examine the ordered trees of $n$ edges that are equipped with a specific ordering on their leaves, with a focus on the deepest vertex containing the maximum distance from a root. By leveraging a combinatorial approach, we derive an explicit formula for the expected value of this vertex distance across all such trees of a fixed size. Furthermore, we analyze the associated probability distribution and establish a central limit theorem governing this quantity.

This study introduces iOCR, a novel method for Optical Character Recognition (OCR) specifically designed to accurately count votes on election ballots. While standard commercial OCR tools are often sufficient for identifying characters, they lack the ability to reliably recognize selected choices in voting contexts. To address this, iOCR leverages the inherent structure of ballots to distinguish between marked and unmarked options. We evaluated iOCR against leading commercial OCR software using real-world data from the 2020 U.S. Presidential Election in Los Angeles County. The results demonstrate that iOCR significantly outperforms existing commercial solutions in accuracy for tallying election results.

This study examines the over-parameterized time series linear model, focusing on its high-dimensional setup where the number of parameters $p$ significantly exceeds the sample size $n$. We analyze the excess risk within a squared loss framework across both stationary and non-stationary regimes, covering scenarios with and without benign overfitting. Our findings reveal that in over-fit contexts, the model achieves an optimal convergence rate of $O(p/n)$ under stationary conditions, whereas it converges at a slower rate of $O(\sqrt{p/n})$ in non-stationary cases. These results highlight how the tension between model complexity and data volume influences both overfitting dynamics and convergence speeds. Additionally, we investigate the impact of different kernel structures on these processes. Finally, we validate our theoretical contributions through simulations and empirical evidence drawn from real-world datasets.

This study examines the storage allocation problem for a decentralized cloud storage marketplace involving an entity with limited capital and a group of risk-averse participants. Each participant exhibits an asymmetric, nonlinear valuation for the resource, while the reallocation entity must determine an optimal distribution of storage capacity that maximizes its own utility. This utility derives from the collective valuations of the agents and the cost associated with executing the reallocation. The entity incurs these costs when agent demands diverge from its initial assignment. By employing a mean-variance framework, we characterize the entity's optimization task and demonstrate that the resulting allocation is unique. Furthermore, we analyze how varying levels of capital and risk aversion influence the utility of the reallocation entity.

This study employs global atmospheric circulation models to analyze how planetary rotation and surface friction influence atmospheric dynamics on Earth-like planets with various atmospheric compositions and thermal forcings. The results demonstrate that, in the absence of meridional temperature gradients, the atmosphere self-organizes into a cyclostrophic super-rotating equatorial jet. This state remains stable across a range of rotation rates, atmospheric chemistries, and heating mechanisms, yet its wind profile and width adjust in response to changes in gravitational acceleration. Conversely, the introduction of a planet-wide temperature gradient triggers a transition to geostrophic turbulence, characterized by chaotic meridional eddies and a significantly reduced equatorial jet. The study further examines the impact of atmospheric opacity on radiative-convective equilibrium and the resulting temperature structure. Finally, it compares the derived circulation patterns with those observed on Venus and Mars, concluding with a framework for classifying terrestrial atmospheric circulation regimes.

We introduce a method for applying continual learning to ImageNet, addressing the challenge of training multiple models from a single 100G image dataset without retraining. Our approach, named Dynamic Learning (DyLe), trains distinct models for each class by utilizing only a small subset of images per class during the initial phase, while leveraging a single image from each category in subsequent steps. This process repeats until all classes have been trained individually. Our method offers two primary advantages: first, it is highly effective, achieving an accuracy of 82.0\% on the ImageNet benchmark—surpassing a baseline model trained with all data by 0.2\%—and outperforming other dynamic learning techniques by approximately 0.5\%. Second, it is remarkably efficient, completing the full training cycle for 1000 classes in just 10 minutes on a single GPU.

We present a complete configuration interaction (CI) simulation of exchange-coupled donor pairs in silicon, employing multi-valley effective mass theory enhanced with full periodic potential corrections for the exchange interaction. This approach explicitly incorporates all excited states and electrons from both valleys, enabling the precise calculation of the Zeeman effect and exchange coupling within the 3d excited states of the two-donor system. Our results demonstrate that valley mixing significantly influences the magnitude and orientation dependence of the exchange interaction, while our derived formulas for the Zeeman effect and coupling are sufficiently precise for current and future experimental setups.

We present a theoretical investigation into the quantum conductance of HgTe quantum wells featuring a critical thickness, where the bulk exists as a gapless metal. Our analysis reveals that even when both quantized subbands within the well are occupied by filled states, a finite conduction persists. This phenomenon is attributed to the asymmetric energy dispersion of Dirac fermions relative to the Dirac point, which prevents complete conductance cancellation. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this quantum conduction exhibits a pronounced dependence on temperature and magnetic fields.

Dynamic Time Division Duplexing (TDD) allows systems to adjust uplink and downlink time slot configurations based on current traffic demands, a technique widely adopted in cellular networks. In a competitive environment involving multiple base stations, the scheduling of uplink and downlink slots becomes a strategic game. This paper introduces a model where each operator functions as a player aiming to maximize individual utility by selecting the most beneficial subframe mix. The proposed utility function integrates both the traffic load and the quality of wireless channels. Within this non-cooperative framework, we demonstrate the existence of a Nash Equilibrium and establish its convergence through replicator dynamic analysis. Furthermore, we define a specific data structure to efficiently compute the proposed game model. Numerical simulations confirm that the derived Nash Equilibrium yields superior performance compared to conventional scheduling approaches.

Hamiltonian Neural Networks (HNNs) are a class of neural network architectures designed for time-series forecasting that guarantee certain physical invariants, such as energy conservation. A key benefit of this design is that they can extrapolate over extended ranges while maintaining these physical constraints. Since the network parameters are differentiable, trajectory derivatives can be computed directly via backpropagation. This study investigates whether the extrapolation of these derivatives benefits from specific choices of Hamiltonian components, focusing on the relationship between the learned network weights and the resulting derivatives. We introduce a novel method to decompose the learned Hamiltonian into its kinetic and potential energy terms. By leveraging this decomposition, we derive a formula for differentiating the predicted outputs without manual differentiation. We validate our approach on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating that it outperforms standard backpropagation in synthetic scenarios and matches its performance on real-world data.

Trustworthiness is a critical attribute for high-stakes machine learning (ML) systems, yet current evaluation methods often fail to address the specific needs of targeted use cases. This paper introduces a human-in-the-loop, multi-agent framework designed to enhance the trustworthiness of an existing system by leveraging agent-generated trust scores and data augmentation strategies. Within this system, agents autonomously select tasks, execute them, and evaluate the resulting outputs. To quantify reliability, the approach employs an agent-specific trust metric that synthesizes output accuracy and behavioral consistency.
